name: set_state
role: Generic "set this thing's state" helper, called as fn(thing, new_state): unless thing+0xe bit 0x10 is set, calls 0x4ed6f0(thing) (removes it from its current state's processing list), writes new_state to thing+0x2c, then calls 0x4ed640(thing) (re-adds it to the new state's list) - used across many classes, not just effects (e.g. 0x445bbb sets a person's state after assigning tribe/type fields); corrects the previous draft of this row, which wrongly described this as an effect-specific dispatcher reading table 0x50afd4 - that dispatch actually lives in a separate function, see 0x50a750

name: order_execute
role: Runs a class-1 person's active command-group order each turn (called as fn(unit) from unit_processing_class_1_person at 0x4d351a, for state 0xA "carrying out an order"): resolves the unit's active command-group id (word at unit+0x9b if nonzero, else unit+0x8b[(byte)unit+0xa6] - corrects an earlier draft of this row, which called 0x938830 a "per-unit lookup table": it is a per-GROUP array shared by every unit currently assigned to that group via 0x436d00/0x436c20, see pop3-rev-analysis.md "Command groups") and, when a real group is assigned, reads that group record's kind byte (group+0x0), subtracts 3, and jumps through a 31-entry table at 0x432d18 covering kinds 3-33 (the odd/even "going to place"/"doing it" pairs) to the per-kind handler, e.g. kind 19 and 21 both call the attack-order handler 0x51A2A0, kind 33 calls the preach-order handler 0x43C7A0; two unread special branches at 0x432a5d/0x432a65 gate on the group record's +0x1 bit 0x1 or the unit's own +0x13 bit 0x10
Only glimpsed this session as the callee for "release a unit's current primary group" (fn(unit,-1), called from 0x436d00 before reassigning unit+0x9b) - not traced

name: group_alloc
role: new command group (Reference table in pop3-rev-analysis.md): fn() -> group_id, scans forward from a rotating cursor (word at 0x96aa78) through the 800-entry 0x938830 array for a slot whose ref-count (+0x2) is 0, wrapping past the array end back to id 1 (id 0 skipped); does not itself set ref-count or any field - see 0x436D00

name: group_assign
role: give a group to a unit (Reference table in pop3-rev-analysis.md): fn(unit, group_id, slot): increments the target group's ref-count (0x938830[group_id]+0x2) and a global active-group counter when it was 0; if slot<0, releases the unit's current primary group via 0x4364d0(unit,-1) then sets unit+0x9b=group_id (primary); else sets unit+0x8b[slot]=group_id (a secondary group slot, meaning of more than one not traced)

name: order_set
role: Writes a command group's shared order ("add an order to a group" in pop3-rev-analysis.md's Reference table; corrects an earlier draft of this row, which called the 1st arg a "unit_id" - it is a group id, see pop3-rev-analysis.md "Command groups"), called as fn(group_id, kind, target_or_pos_ptr, extra_flags): writes into that group's 10-byte slot in the 0x938830 array (slot = group_id*10 + 0x938830) - if the slot already holds this exact kind AND the same target/position dword at slot+0x6, it is a complete no-op (returns immediately, verified: no position-rounding or state change happens on this path); otherwise sets slot+0x0 = kind, ORs extra_flags into slot+0x1, copies *target_or_pos_ptr into slot+0x6, then derives a snapped/line-of-sight-adjusted position (per-kind flags DWORD from a table at 0x5a7dc0+kind*22+0xa, confirmed stride 22 bytes/kind this session, select rounding via 0x4044b0 and a per-direction table at 0x8a03e4) back into slot+0x6/+0x8; at the very end, if that same per-kind flags DWORD has bit 0x80000 set and the slot's own target id resolves (table 0x890390) to a live unit whose own +0x9d field has bit 0x80 set, it OVERWRITES the slot's kind to 0xA (10) while keeping the same target id; of its ~37 call sites, most pass extra_flags=0 (via an explicitly-zeroed register) or the literal 0x20 (0x20 is confirmed this session: 0x51FF60 skips the auto-attack-radius lookup for any group with flags bit 0x20 set); only one call site found this session (0x41cd6f, in an unrelated per-tribe function 0x41cc20 using order kind 0x1c/28) passes the literal 0x40 that 0x51C3C0 checks for preacher targeting - the call site that sets 0x40 for an actual preach order (if any) was not found and is the next concrete lead for "Preacher conversion"

name: order_building_approach
role: Order handler shared by kinds 31 and 32 (order_execute's table entries for both point here), called as fn(unit, order): a 5-substate approach-and-wait machine (jump table at 0x43ABD8, unit substate at +0x2d) - substates 1-2 walk to within ~0x538/0xc units of the order's position (0x43A310 checks line of sight/occupancy), substate 3 is a ~separator wait, substate 4 runs an RNG roll (LCG at 0x89BC72) each turn against odds from a per-type table at 0x59DF44 indexed by unit+0x33, and on success plays an animation (0x4D4040, ids 0x5F/0x61 seen) and a tribe-relative UI sound (0x48A050, id 0x33 for the human player's own tribe else 0xBD) with a disguise-like flag (unit+0xb2 bit 0) and ~840-turn (0x348) duration; no attacker/target-type branch was found in this function, so kind 31 vs 32 (disguise vs the preacher's building visit) likely differ only in data (the per-type table at 0x59DF44), not in code path - the actual preacher-specific payoff (if any) is not in this function and remains unlocated

name: preach_order_handler
role: Preach order (kind 33) per-turn handler, called as fn(preacher) from order_execute's (0x432590) kind-dispatch table - takes a 2nd "order slot" arg by the same convention as other kind handlers but never reads it; instead resolves its own target live each call from the preacher's own +0x89 field (seeded from +0x72 on first entry) via unit table 0x890390, into a local "target" pointer (called edi below, NOT the order slot): while preacher substate (preacher+0x2d) is 1 "approaching", checks the target's building occupancy against a population-cap-like pair of fields (building+0x96 vs +0x9a via building lookup 0x508f70) and, failing that, on closing to ~12 units sets substate 2 (or 4 if target+0x76 == 0x99); substates 1-3 walk toward the target, substates 4-8 stop and face it (0x4458d0); substates (1-9 remapped via 0x43d010) and (2-9) branch through two more inline jump tables at 0x43d004/0x43d01c; the terminal substate-8 body (0x43cd77) is the actual payoff: plays sound 0x9f on the TARGET, sets the target's own state (target+0x2c) to 5, and rewrites the target's internal animation-sequence kinds to 0x98/0x9b/0x99 over 40 ticks via 0x4f14b0 (same helper also used on the preacher's own substates elsewhere in this function, likely a generic "overlay effect sequence" setter, not an order) - this is the confirmed link from the preach order to the target, but it sets state 5, not the "struck" state 3 from pop3-rev-analysis.md "Preacher conversion"; see 0x4d6970 for why state 5 is probably unrelated to conversion, and 0x51c3c0 for the actual (still unfound) state-3 trigger candidate

name: process_tribe_cmd
role: The giant player-command dispatcher (Ghidra's own name, 0x43e8e0-0x4422bf; pop3-rev-analysis.md "Commands"); only one case was looked at this session: command id 0x41 (byte[cmd+0xc]-0xc, remapped via byte table 0x4423f0 to index 26, dispatch table 0x4422c0), at 0x43f3dc-0x43f41e, which ORs 0x8 into the issuing tribe's +0x93d flags (`or DWORD[tribe+0x93d],0x8`) - the "spells are free" cheat/debug flag (see 0x4c14c0); the other ~120 cases are uncatalogued

name: init_unit_type_11
role: Per-type init dispatcher for a class-11 spell unit (Ghidra's own name); the cast-cost path (0x4c16d6) tests tribe+0x93d bit 0x8 and, only when clear, calls 0x41a4f0 (add_mana, documented in pop3-rev-analysis.md) with a negated cost to actually deduct it - this is hard confirmation that tribe+0x93d bit 0x8 means "spells are free" (matches the Tribe record table in pop3-rev-analysis.md), not the unrelated "sees invisible people?" guess in that doc's Status markers section, which this session disproves

Only looked at for its own tribe+0x93d bit 0x8 check (0x4c2947), which guards a read of the per-spell constant table at 0x5a80d0+spell*0x3e+0x1a (likely a per-spell charge-cost flag) the same way 0x4c14c0 guards the mana deduction - second confirmation this turn that the bit means "spells are free"; the rest of the function (what it does with that table byte) was not read

unit_processing_class_1_person's state-5 per-turn handler (table 0x4d3d18, index state-1): resolves a reference unit live from this person's own +0x72 field; while present and within 120 units on both axes, counts down a timer at +0x70 and, each turn while close, stores an RNG value (LCG at 0x89d178) scaled by a per-type odds table (0x5a7067) into +0x7b (looks like an idle-animation-variant pick, not a pass/fail roll); on timer expiry (or no reference unit) returns a per-type animation/sound id from table 0x5a7064 (shaman special-cased to 0x27) - reads as a generic "idle near a reference unit" behaviour with no write to this person's own state (+0x2c), so it is likely unrelated to "Preacher conversion" despite 0x43C7A0 putting its target into this same state 5

name: alloc_unit
role: Allocates a unit: alloc_unit(class, type, tribe, pos*); args pushed in reverse order

name: init_unit_type_7
role: Per-type init dispatcher for a class-7 effect (Ghidra's own name; called as fn(effect)): reads effect+0x2b (type), subtracts 1, and jumps through the 0x5c-entry table at 0x50a59c to the per-type init case; most cases seen this session end by calling 0x401b10 (set_state) to move the effect into its first running state
Per-type init dispatch table for effects (class 7 units), indexed by type-1, used by 0x509c10 (init_unit_type_7)

name: unit_processing_class_7_effect
role: Per-state per-turn dispatcher for a class-7 effect (Ghidra's own name; called as fn(effect)): reads effect+0x2c (state), subtracts 1, and jumps through the 0x4e-entry table at 0x50afd4 to the per-state case; many cases call 0x401b10 (set_state) to advance to the next state
Per-state per-turn dispatch table for effects (class 7 units), indexed by state-1, used by 0x50a750 (unit_processing_class_7_effect)

name: attack_order_handler
role: The attack-order handler (kinds 19/21, pop3-rev-analysis.md "Starting a melee"/"Pre-fight"); only newly looked at this session for its calls to 0x51c3c0 (at 0x51a601, 0x51a6f1, 0x51a85a, 0x51bc04) which gate whether a scanned/ordered target is a legal opponent - the rest of the function is already covered in the spec doc and not re-traced here

name: attack_target_eligibility
role: Per-attacker-type "can I fight this" dispatcher, called as fn(attacker_unit, order_or_candidate_record, result_word_ptr, extra) from the attack-order handler (0x51A2A0): record+0x0==0x1c (kind 28) short-circuits straight to a shared generic path; else dispatches on attacker type (+0x2b): firewarrior (6) to 0x51D0B0, preacher (4) to 0x51CE50, everything else to the generic 0x51C4C0; the shared path resolves the record's target id (+0x6) to a live unit via table 0x890390 and, only when that target's class (+0x2a) is 1 (person), applies one gate relevant to conversion: if the attacker is a preacher (type 4) and the found target is NOT also a preacher, the attempt is rejected unless record+0x1 bit 0x40 is set - this flag is the likely master switch for "preacher may engage a non-preacher target" (for conversion rather than ordinary melee), but what sets it is not yet traced (prime lead for the next session)

name: preacher_person_scan
role: Preacher/shaman person-target scan, called from 0x51C3C0 when the attacker is a preacher: walks a grid of cells around the position packed at record+0x6/+0x8 (the exact radius/stepping was not fully re-derived - corrects an earlier draft's confident "3x3 then expanding" claim; what is confirmed is each visited cell is followed via the live unit table 0x890390 and the per-cell linked list at unit+0x20) and keeps the nearest candidate whose class (+0x2a) is 1 (person) and whose type (+0x2b) is 4 (preacher) or 7 (shaman) - i.e. confirms preachers only ever melee other preachers/shamans this way; ordinary units are never returned as a person-fight target here, matching pop3-rev-analysis.md "preachers and shamans fight each other in melee like anyone else, no conversion on a person match" (same rule as the doc's 0x51EC80, not yet confirmed to be the identical function)

name: preacher_auto_scan
role: The preacher's own per-turn auto-attack scan (pop3-rev-analysis.md "Preacher conversion"'s "preacher's own scan"), called as fn(preacher_unit): runs two building/person detection scans (0x51F030, not fully read) and, if a living person candidate is found (resolved through table 0x890390: its +0xc bit 0x1 clear and its +0x2a byte nonzero - corrects an earlier draft of this row that mislabeled which offset is which), allocates a new order via 0x436C20 and starts it with 0x438730(order_id, kind=0x15, &candidate_pos, 0x20) - an ordinary attack order, same kind as any melee; if instead a building candidate is found with no person candidate, it starts 0x438730(order_id, kind=0x20, &own_pos, 0x20) - confirms pop3-rev-analysis.md's guessed "kind 0x20 pushed" for the building case, but kind 0x20's handler (0x43A4D0, see below) turns out to be shared with disguise, not a distinct conversion routine, so the actual building-side conversion trigger is still unlocated

The command-group array: a fixed pool of 800 shared order records, NOT a per-unit table (corrects two earlier drafts of this row: it is indexed by a GROUP id, not a unit id - see pop3-rev-analysis.md "Command groups"). 10-byte records at 0x938830 + group_id*10: kind byte @0, caller-supplied flag bits OR'd in @+0x1 (0x20 = skip the auto-attack-radius lookup in 0x51FF60; 0x40 = the still-unexplained "preacher may engage a non-preacher target" switch checked by 0x51C3C0), a word ref-count @+0x2 (how many units point at this group; 0 = free slot, scanned for by the allocator 0x436C20), a target-id/position DWORD @+0x6; written by 0x438730 (order_set); a unit's own word fields +0x9b (primary group) or +0x8b[+0xa6] (secondary group slots, set by 0x436D00, released by 0x4364D0) select which group record it runs via order_execute (0x432590); +0x1 bit 0x1 and the unit's own +0x13 bit 0x10 flag select two special-case branches in order_execute (0x432a5d/0x432a65, still unread); cited in pop3-rev-analysis.md "Preacher conversion" as holding values 0x11/0x1f/0x20 (kinds 17/31/32) on preachee-related state 23/24 checks, not re-verified this session
